commit.message:
Apply feature overrides when restarting the app-server daemon (#53751)

## Why

`codex app-server daemon restart` previously reused saved settings without applying feature flags supplied on the command line.

## What changed

Apply `--enable`, `--disable`, and boolean `-c features.*` overrides during an explicit restart and persist them for subsequent restarts. Accept nested `enabled` values, normalize feature aliases, and replace conflicting saved aliases while preserving unrelated settings.

Reject invalid feature toggles before stopping the daemon or saving settings.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for overrides on stopped and running daemons, alias replacement, preservation of saved settings, restarts without flags, and rejection of non-toggle keys without interrupting the running daemon.

GitOrigin-RevId: 14a657bc4758b9c248e363f9dac58f8887070a04

Prefer remote Visualize installs over the bundled plugin (#53747)

## What changed

When the remote global catalog is active, let a cached `visualize@openai-curated-remote` install supersede `visualize@openai-bundled`, matching the existing Sites behavior. A disabled remote install also suppresses the bundled plugin; a missing remote bundle preserves the bundled fallback.

## Testing

Extend the agent-turn compatibility tests to cover Visualize with enabled, disabled, and missing remote bundles, asserting which skills appear in the developer prompt.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7d0cc564189249e597d5bd29b5800353d89a9060

Remove `modelSlug` from the latest-model resolver output (#53745)

## What changed

Update the OpenAI docs sample resolver to return only `model`, `migrationGuideUrl`, and `promptingGuideUrl`, and remove the model-to-slug conversion helper.

GitOrigin-RevId: d7cea29ff8121b1a4df3b062d54dcbed6a1589bd

Acquire and cache opt-in executor capability inventories via V2 (#53736)

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `executor_capability_discovery_v2` feature to acquire `capabilities/discoverV2` inventories from supporting remote executors using each selected environment's working directory and sandbox.
- Share snapshots with MCP and world-state contributors and skill providers without activating discovered plugins or publishing discovered skills to the model.
- Cache inventories by environment instance, executor session, working directory, and sandbox. Coalesce concurrent requests, refresh the cache at turn start, retry transient failures, and refresh MCP projections after recovery.
- Resolve the system skills root in the executor and pass it explicitly to capability location discovery.

## Testing

Add coverage for feature gating, unsupported executors, inert inventories, cache reuse and eviction, turn refreshes, failure recovery, executor replacement, and system skill locations.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1bdca28fa7f17622b27e2713ab3dcc0c13426889

Default Guardian v2 async classification to conversation mode (#53733)

## What changed

Use `conversation` when neither a local `async_classifier_mode` override nor a model default specifies a mode. Keep `snapshot` available as an explicit override and update the configuration documentation and schema to describe the new fallback.

## Testing

Expand configuration tests to cover all local override and model default combinations. Update app-server approval tests to exercise conversation mode without an explicit override, and explicitly select snapshot mode in tests that depend on it.

GitOrigin-RevId: a62479a3f6454bf28d589373a236d8b0ab5023b9

Reuse compiled search patterns across compressed rollouts (#53732)

## Why

Compressed rollout searches recompiled the same query patterns for every file.

## What changed

Lazily compile and reuse the JSON-escaped and content search patterns across each scan, including the fallback scan when `ripgrep` is unavailable. Keep compilation failures within the existing per-file error handling and open files before compiling patterns.

## Testing

Add regression coverage verifying that an oversized query does not fail the compressed rollout scan and that a missing file still returns `NotFound` before query compilation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0d41cbca6e1f716fc234c268493d8dd94c34975e

Preserve the remote cwd filter in the in-app resume picker (#53728)

## Why

Opening the in-app resume picker created a new app-server session without the active session's remote working directory override, dropping the remote directory filter from the thread list.

## What changed

Pass the active session's remote working directory override to the picker session so its `thread/list` request retains the `cwd` filter.

## Testing

Add a regression test that opens the in-app picker against a recording remote server and verifies that `thread/list` includes the remote working directory in `cwd`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0073ed77e9d9b0ffdd647fcb9f157d20ea2aa599

Render Markdown web links as labels in Rex (#53725)

## What changed

Select label-only web link rendering when `TERM_PROGRAM` is `rex`, matched case-insensitively. Preserve the existing visible-destination fallback for multiplexers and `dumb`, `screen`, or `tmux` terminal modes.

## Testing

Add a regression test verifying that Rex renders `[label](https://example.com)` with the label-only policy.

GitOrigin-RevId: 615ca6186d84fc17cef9286e75848877b542b6ab

Wire V2 capability discovery through exec-server RPC (#53723)

## What changed

- Register `capabilities/discoverV2` for initialized sessions and expose it through `ExecServerClient` and remote `Environment` APIs, checking executor support before calling it.
- Reuse startup discovery locations and retry failed prewarming on demand. Replay discovery once after executor recovery while preserving the request parameters.
- Track whether all required filesystem watches registered successfully and reload locations and metadata on each request when registration fails.

## Testing

Add coverage for RPC metadata refresh, omission of skill instruction bodies, sandbox isolation, startup scan recovery, disconnect replay, and successful or failed watch registration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 726e8f7e8b4d835b877f31d1d8a9f8eea1ad9c8b

Enable Cyber access programs for API-key sessions by default (#53717)

## What changed

- Default `features.api_key_cyber_access_programs` to `true` and allow `codex exec` to select Daybreak with an OpenAI API key. Select the advertised standard program when `daybreak=false`, while respecting explicit feature opt-outs.
- Resolve API-key eligibility for TUI background turns from the target thread's feature settings, including project opt-outs. Omit access-program overrides when the server cannot report those settings.
- Preserve automatic server treatment for unlisted models and missing or empty Cyber program metadata in exec and TUI. Continue rejecting Daybreak when a nonempty program list does not offer it.

## Testing

Update regression coverage for API-key Daybreak selection, the off override, explicit opt-outs, resumed sessions, target-thread settings, and missing model metadata.

GitOrigin-RevId: f3cf7bd95a2754d4b4281bc70b18c7da4b177552

Separate MCP sandbox policy from launcher metadata (#53709)

## Why

MCP servers must forward sandbox policy unchanged to `codex sandbox --sandbox-state-json`, while interpreting launcher information to find the Codex CLI. Keep those contracts separate so consumers can preserve unknown policy fields.

## What changed

- Accept the experimental `codex/sandbox-state` capability alongside the deprecated `codex/sandbox-state-meta` capability, and send identical policy values under both `_meta` keys.
- Move `codexExecutable` out of the policy into `codex/sandbox-launcher`, supplied only when a verified CLI path is available for a local stdio server.
- Replace stale sandbox metadata while retaining unrelated entries, and remove stale launcher metadata when no launcher is available.
- Document the metadata contract and how servers should forward policy and retain authority for long-lived subprocesses.

## Testing

Update unit and integration coverage for policy serialization, identical state aliases, launcher availability across execution environments, and stale metadata replacement.

GitOrigin-RevId: e544c06e6e023953b1fc8069b7b1affa065262d1

Preserve URLs and email addresses during external agent migration (#53706)

## Why

Rewriting source agent names and instruction filenames inside URLs and email addresses can change their destinations when importing external agent content.

## What changed

Use `linkify` to preserve recognized URLs and email addresses while rewriting surrounding text, including Markdown link labels and titles. Continue migrating instruction filename references to `AGENTS.md`, including relative links and references with line or column suffixes.

## Testing

Add rewrite coverage for URLs, email addresses, Markdown links, and surrounding Unicode text. Extend skill import and app-server configuration import tests to verify that link labels migrate while URL destinations remain unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: c4d210a287c99b6440438c99527364d379c568bd

Enable CLI Daybreak by default and enforce background-turn eligibility (#53701)

## What changed

- Mark `cli_daybreak` as stable and enable it by default.
- Apply Daybreak to background turns only for eligible OpenAI accounts, allowing API-key accounts when `api_key_cyber_access_programs` is enabled. Preserve saved settings for ineligible accounts and report account lookup failures when Daybreak is enabled for the OpenAI provider.
- Skip inheriting Daybreak configuration when the app server does not support reading effective configuration.

## Testing

Expand dynamic-tool request tests to cover the feature toggle, ChatGPT and API-key authentication, API-key program eligibility, and unsupported configuration reads.

GitOrigin-RevId: 55a57315c9f527f977dd8305ea62d4096ed7dae9

Cancel Guardian V2 classifications that exceed the tool-call lag window (#53699)

## Why

Pending classifications can outlive the `max_tool_call_lag` window in which their scores are reusable, keeping metadata waits or classifier transports active after the result becomes stale.

## What changed

- Expire pending classifications when tool-call progress exceeds the configured lag allowance, preserving the wrapper discount while nested code-mode actions remain active.
- Cancel metadata waits and sampling in snapshot and conversation modes, including snapshot response drains after an early score.
- Treat expiry as supersession, preserving cached scores and the last completed conversation checkpoint and transcript cursor.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for lag boundaries, active wrapper discounts, transport cancellation before and after early scores, expired requests skipping preparation, and conversation history and transcript deltas surviving cancellation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 892ff13a05fd2b1573cef9842b934d1fc865d951

Interrupt and drain canceled classifier responses before socket reuse (#53698)

## Why

Canceled classifier requests need bounded cleanup that preserves received token usage and returns only safe WebSocket connections to the pool.

## What changed

- Own classifier response streams and connection leases together, interrupting dropped responses with a one-second cleanup deadline.
- Require a matching interruption acknowledgement and response completion before reusing a canceled response's socket. Retire sockets on rejection, invalid acknowledgements, or timeout while preserving any received completion and token usage.
- Skip requests canceled before dispatch and return their unused sockets to the pool.
- Distinguish cancellation from ordinary steering, which continues draining without requiring an interruption acknowledgement.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for cancellation, acknowledgement ordering and failures, cleanup timeouts, socket reuse, and token accounting under backpressure. Extend steering tests to cover rejected and missing acknowledgements.

GitOrigin-RevId: c4e7aac49d36cea2c2d0e9f2ba5f6147f67471dd

Add keyboard selection support to the transcript view (#53693)

## What changed

Add transcript select-mode state with an underlined cursor, grapheme-aware movement via arrow keys or `h`/`j`/`k`/`l`, and vertical movement that preserves the preferred display column. Support marking with `v`, Space, or Shift-arrow keys and copying through the existing selection machinery.

Keep the displayed transcript snapshot and reading position paused during selection and after exiting the mode. Add entry and exit methods; this change does not yet bind mode entry to a user-facing key.

## Testing

Add unit tests for initial cursor placement, movement across empty lines and entry boundaries, wrapped text, preferred-column preservation, and Enter behavior with and without a marked range.

GitOrigin-RevId: e5bc380ea0eb6e2c6157ba73ac063d548a7de145

Account for replay caches in encrypted compaction budgets (#53691)

## Why

Encrypted compaction payloads can include sampled-token replay caches that increase their size roughly threefold. Budgeting them as ordinary text can reject checkpoints that fit the model context budget.

## What changed

Use a shared estimate of one token per twelve ciphertext bytes, rounded up, for encrypted `Compaction` and `ContextCompaction` items in history and Guardian context budgeting. Guardian continues to count framing and metadata separately.

Check parent compactions against the configured token budget and a separate hard wire-size limit. Preserve the complete encrypted checkpoint when it fits. The token estimate remains a heuristic and can underestimate legacy checkpoints without replay caches.

## Testing

Add coverage for token-estimate rounding, parent compaction token and wire-size limits, and reviewer continuation with a cached compaction preserved intact.

GitOrigin-RevId: cc18ca29802491865167eef992830efcf93d97da

Constrain API-key model access programs to server support (#53689)

## Why

Servers can advertise cyber access programs without accepting them for API-key accounts. The TUI must account for server support before exposing those programs.

## What changed

- Check `features.api_key_cyber_access_programs` at startup and when loading models for API-key accounts, clearing `available_access_programs` when forwarding is unavailable.
- Use thread-scoped feature settings after thread creation and honor feature requirements and CLI overrides at startup.
- Refresh account-scoped models when switching to or from API-key authentication or changing API-key thread context, clearing cached access programs while the refresh is pending.

## Testing

Extend session tests to cover enabled and disabled server settings, CLI overrides, and catalog filtering before and after thread creation. Update account-change tests to handle the model refresh.

GitOrigin-RevId: c80de30a0063b84949098d137715d8678bd70587

Preserve inherited context in prediction forks (#53678)

## Why

Prediction forks need to retain their parent's context even when it exceeds the automatic compaction threshold. Compaction or context resets can otherwise replace the history used for the prediction.

## What changed

- Apply a thread-local `AutoCompactionDisabled` policy to experimental prediction forks without changing model or skill budgets.
- Skip automatic compaction before, during, and after turns, including context-limit recovery, and suppress new token-budget reminders.
- Reject `new_context` requests for these threads and report context-limit failures without compacting their history.

## Testing

Add regression tests for legacy and paginated prediction forks across compaction thresholds, unchanged parent compaction and skill/tool inputs, context-limit failures, and rejected context resets. Add a request-history snapshot verifying inherited context and reminders survive without compaction or additional reminders after a tool call.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7df374287f4142f776981bb6c22e5caa564d74a5

Publish Rust releases with the GitHub CLI (#53673)

## What changed

Replace `softprops/action-gh-release` in `.github/workflows/rust-release.yml` with explicit `gh` commands:

- Look up the release by tag, including drafts, and fail on API errors.
- Create stable releases as drafts until assets are uploaded. Create prereleases directly to preserve prerelease events.
- Upload sorted assets with `--clobber`, then publish the release with the configured title, notes, prerelease status, and latest status.
- Cap release notes at 124,999 characters, including a trailing newline.

GitOrigin-RevId: f343e4f265b06e047d85fe5a2b89a92690c7a7fb

Keep discovered Apps tools available during startup recovery (#53672)

## Why

A transient Apps MCP startup failure can remove cached tools that the model has already discovered, preventing a later Code Mode invocation from using them.

## What changed

Keep cached Apps tools in the model's tool catalog while startup recovery runs. Let invocation readiness start or join a shared retry before acquiring the tool execution lock, while tool discovery remains nonblocking. Keep recovery running if a waiting invocation is cancelled.

## Testing

Extend connection-manager tests to cover cached tool bindings and shared recovery. Add a Code Mode regression test that discovers a cached Calendar tool, invokes it after startup fails, and verifies that it succeeds after recovery while unrelated tools remain able to execute.

GitOrigin-RevId: e888501a1050884a50a473e71b893cf6672fe256

Account for token usage from incomplete responses (#53670)

## Why

Terminal `response.incomplete` errors discard reported token usage. Counting that usage as a new context baseline can also double-count input and trigger unnecessary compaction on the next turn.

## What changed

- Carry the response ID and valid reported usage with incomplete-response errors.
- Record usage for sampling and foreground compaction in cumulative totals, rollout records, budgets, and token-usage contributors without replacing the context baseline. Preserve the original terminal error, including when accounting exhausts the budget or cancellation races the error.
- Charge incomplete background compaction requests to the rollout budget without publishing foreground token usage.
- Ignore missing or malformed usage rather than estimating it.

## Testing

Extend coverage for SSE and WebSocket incomplete responses, rollout usage records, compaction accounting, deferred token-count events, and token-usage contributors. Add regressions for unnecessary compaction on the next turn and background compaction publishing foreground usage.

GitOrigin-RevId: bf1ee6df3912052ab7c19e1c6af8ad3dc4b07675

Improve remote exec-server test startup diagnostics (#53668)

## Why

The remote exec-server parent-lifetime test can hide an early process exit behind a connection timeout, making startup failures harder to diagnose.

## What changed

- Race the WebSocket connection against the child process exiting so startup exits are reported immediately.
- Include the registration request count and child status when attachment fails, without inspecting request headers or bodies containing authentication data.
- Enable remote exec-server info logging in the test while keeping other logs at error level.

GitOrigin-RevId: 75739fc93d7f28ba0a3f447a14d4d20b2dbdfd14

Extract shared multi-agent v2 thread spawning (#53660)

## What changed

Move child configuration, task path construction, fork usage hints, and backend spawning into `core::thread_spawn`. Add request, result, and error types that distinguish preparation failures from backend errors.

Route the v2 `spawn_agent` handler through the shared helper while retaining tool-specific telemetry, activity events, and response formatting in the handler.

GitOrigin-RevId: a09a8f66beb41c1403220750d236a12717dbfc6c

Share hook configuration across cloned hook views (#53657)

## Why

`with_executor_hooks` clones the hook registry to create an executor-specific view. Copying the configured handlers, plugin sources, and diagnostics on every clone is unnecessary when that configuration is unchanged.

## What changed

Store hook configuration in `Arc`-backed collections and use copy-on-write when replacing executor-scoped handlers. Skip handler mutation when there are no executor hooks to add or remove.

## Testing

Extend the executor hook registration test to verify that updating a cloned engine leaves the previous engine's handlers unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6b188ca6ca21772ccd7336344d98c023f769834e

Keep spawned children provisional until the spawn result returns (#53654)

## Why

Cancellation after initial input admission could leave a child registered even though the spawn caller had not received its result.

## What changed

Resolve the child's status and configuration before committing reservations and releasing provisional ownership. This keeps cancellation cleanup active through the final awaits and lets the spawn result return without yielding after commitment. Cancellation after the result returns does not retract the accepted child.

## Testing

Add a regression test that cancels spawn during the final status lookup after input admission and verifies that the child is unregistered, terminated, and unloaded, and that shutdown completes. Extend the provisional-child cancellation test to cover both native V1 and V2 callers.

GitOrigin-RevId: 028b873ad4c1fac2c4b5d1dc823b4561ff19e6bf

Add an environment API key fallback for Guardian Decisions (#53633)

## What changed

Allow Guardian Decisions to use `OPENAI_API_KEY` when the default `openai` provider has no custom base URL and neither `CODEX_GUARDIAN_DECISIONS_API_KEY` nor a cached API key is available. Preserve cached API key precedence over the environment fallback.

Report missing credentials as `credentials_unavailable` instead of `provider_error` in Decisions failure metrics.

## Testing

Add tests for cached API key precedence and the environment fallback with ChatGPT authentication. Run each test in a child process to isolate environment changes.

GitOrigin-RevId: fbb772dcb9287d9e1be1b34292ad9bdffeb3d6b3

Stabilize write ordering in the shared message board scenario (#53632)

## Why

Non-parallel tool calls can acquire their lock in either order, making the shared board scenario's `last_message_id` snapshot nondeterministic.

## What changed

Send each `collaboration.post` call in a separate mocked response to order the writes before snapshotting. Update the `board_connections` snapshot and expected request count from 15 to 17 to reflect the additional responses.

GitOrigin-RevId: a290a01f5071a2081d4d0b1531b1b31bfbb8a6e6

Materialize the thread before testing a discovered daemon restart (#53631)

Empty drafts need not survive a daemon restart. Update the `discovered`
scenario in `codex-rs/cli/tests/daemon_startup.rs` to rename the thread before
restarting the daemon and include `thread-name` in the status line. Wait for
the confirmed footer name before issuing `/daemon` so the test proceeds only
after the thread is materialized.

GitOrigin-RevId: a91508582826fa1bd0cc7b89d9a1af7e8b4e1999

Record truncation metrics for accepted Guardian review inputs (#53628)

## What changed

Emit `codex.guardian.review.truncation` counts and `codex.guardian.review.truncation.bytes` histograms after successful input finalization. Aggregate observations across reduction stages by component and disposition (`truncated` or `omitted`), recording original, retained, and omitted byte totals. Exclude feasibility checks and failed retries from loss telemetry.

Keep blocking command-hook cancellation fixtures in the local environment and use double quotes for the Python command.

## Testing

Add metric-export tests covering aggregation across multiple reductions, separate truncation and omission totals, no loss metrics for rejected inputs, and no duplicate reporting on repeated finalization.

GitOrigin-RevId: 69182fc7afe230be69dd2469caedb5ae4494947b

Preserve remote exec output until it is collected (#53622)

## Why

Remote process exit can arrive before the final output, and inherited pipes can keep the output stream open after exit. Removing the session at exit can lose output that should remain available to `write_stdin` polls.

## What changed

- Retain remote sessions with open or unread output after exit, including early exits and cancelled initial collection.
- Collect pending output when `write_stdin` races with exit, skipping stdin writes once remote exit is known.
- After initial collection finishes and the process exits, allow a five-second grace period before a final background read. Respect active polling deadlines and keep later polls available while that read recovers retained output.
- Let explicit termination stop output collection even when the process has already exited, and install the exit watcher before cancellable cleanup.

## Testing

Extend remote process event tests to cover output arriving after the initial yield, polling during a delayed final read, active polls exceeding the background grace period, resumable cancellation, and termination before the initial yield.

GitOrigin-RevId: b1671fad8b61a2cdecf7cf9fdf92e57c028c7af8

Reuse background results for remote V2 compaction (#53620)

## What changed

- Await a compatible pending background request when foreground compaction is needed, and share the result installation path with foreground requests.
- Validate the captured history generation, prefix length, model, and authentication owner before installing a prepared result. Fall back to foreground compaction when required if the result is rejected.
- Replace only the captured history prefix, preserving later messages, retained tool outputs, goal edits, and the current world-state baseline. Record installation analytics and completion events only after a result is installed.

GitOrigin-RevId: 798963f2fc603c3febba2c21eafa1bcb094b3ebf

Allow hiding native tools while retaining the multi-agent V2 runtime (#53617)

## What changed

Add `features.multi_agent_v2.disable_native_tools` to hide native multi-agent tools while keeping the V2 runtime and its instructions enabled for host-provided tools. The option defaults to `false`, preserving existing tool exposure.

## Testing

Extend configuration parsing tests for the new option and parameterize the multi-agent catalog scenario to cover both settings. Add a snapshot showing native tools are absent while the V2 runtime and instructions remain enabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: 21a53584d2395bb678813c876a8b7927bea61c90

Add infrastructure for speculative remote V2 compaction (#53614)

## What changed

- Capture history, prompt metadata, routing state, authentication ownership, and context-window identity for background compaction requests.
- Send background requests over HTTP while preserving foreground routing, and retain the latest candidate in session memory.
- Add feature and threshold eligibility checks and deduplicate attempts by history version, model, compaction hash, and authentication ownership.
- Cancel and drain background tasks during session shutdown, preserving completed usage accounting.

The background launch helper is not yet connected to the turn loop.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0e5e6ab7dac4d98a836733668a775ac48b5a59f1

Prepare compaction helpers for background requests (#53606)

## What changed

- Extract an HTTP Responses executor that can run without owning a turn's WebSocket state, with optional authentication-owner checks.
- Add cancellation-aware compaction output collection that records background token usage against the rollout budget.
- Support installing a compacted history prefix while preserving later history items and placing initial context around real user or agent messages.
- Allow callers to supply a context window for history trimming and a captured window for compaction request metadata.

GitOrigin-RevId: 29f3ca0ae8841f295058feb207e3a225af9a1487

Add async compaction feature configuration (#53595)

## What changed

Register the disabled-by-default `async_compaction` feature and accept either a boolean or a `[features.async_compaction]` table. Add `model_async_compact_threshold_percent` with a default of 65 and a valid range of 1–100, validated even when the feature is disabled. Setting a threshold alone does not enable the feature.

Expose the threshold in the runtime configuration and update the JSON schema for both configuration forms.

## Testing

Add configuration loader tests covering boolean and table forms, default and custom thresholds, explicit enablement, and rejection of out-of-range values.

GitOrigin-RevId: cf33de76878e7044bc8cf5d146375a07ea9eb078

Deduplicate TUI modifier handling and terminal color caching (#53556)

## What changed

- Reuse `custom_terminal::ModifierDiff` when writing history spans.
- Share the terminal default-color probe and cache implementation between Unix and Windows.

Both changes remove duplicate implementations while preserving existing behavior.

GitOrigin-RevId: 35f8d77ade972b791c6beac0678d2fe2be3aa763

Reject duplicate Host headers in the network proxy (#53506)

## Why

Policy evaluation and upstream parsers must not select different `Host` field lines from the same request.

## What changed

Return `400 Bad Request` for multiple `Host` headers, including identical values, before policy evaluation, upstream forwarding, or Unix socket routing. Apply the check to both plain HTTP requests and `CONNECT` requests.

## Testing

Add regression tests covering identical and conflicting headers in origin-form, absolute-form, and `CONNECT` requests, verifying rejection without an upstream connection. Also cover single-header forwarding and rejection before Unix socket routing.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8ec95171e120f784629d3121b9a1bedbaf88e7cd

Preserve pending Effects toggles across save refreshes (#53496)

## Why

Saving an Effects preference refreshes the picker. When users toggle repeatedly before saves finish, that refresh can discard newer choices and cause subsequent toggles to use stale values.

## What changed

- Update Effects checkboxes immediately and track pending saves per row, preserving newer choices when an earlier save takes effect.
- Preserve pending Composer stars choices while Animations disables the row, and clear pending state on a regular panel refresh.
- Use the shared list toggle handling for Effects, including Space support, while giving configured key bindings precedence over Space toggling.

## Testing

Add regression tests for repeated toggles across save refreshes, pending Composer stars choices while disabled, clearing pending state, and a Space cancel binding taking precedence over toggling. Update the Effects picker snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: 847dcc2dfd40448c7adc56c8c40879db28b1fc39

Update `quinn-proto` to 0.11.18 (#53485)

## What changed

Update `codex-rs/Cargo.lock` and `MODULE.bazel.lock` for `quinn-proto` 0.11.18, replacing 0.11.15. Refresh its resolved dependencies to use `rand` 0.10.1 and `getrandom` 0.4.2, and add `rand_pcg` 0.10.2.

GitOrigin-RevId: 642bdeccbff8017f2f97b640a2b2c48294c97bba

Prefer the Windows clipboard and bound copy attempts on WSL (#53453)

## Why

WSLg clipboard initialization can block indefinitely, and PowerShell clipboard writes can stall while receiving input or exiting. These stalls can prevent subsequent TUI copy requests from completing.

## What changed

- Try the Windows clipboard first for `/copy` and `Ctrl+O` on WSL, falling back to the native clipboard and terminal delivery when needed.
- Give Windows executable discovery and writing a shared five-second deadline, with a separate one-second deadline for native clipboard setup. Reuse pending setup tasks after timeouts to avoid accumulating blocked threads.
- Launch PowerShell through a native shell and stop its process group on write failures or timeouts. Reap the writer before returning so an older copy cannot overwrite a newer one, and suppress stderr that could expose clipboard contents.

## Testing

Add tests for command compatibility, large Unicode input, expired requests, and cleanup of stalled writers and subprocesses. Update routing tests to cover Windows-first copying and native fallback with HTML and clipboard leases.

GitOrigin-RevId: 218c8541a169a16536db0370455e076a31a42b1f

Close input admission while a turn finishes recording (#53452)

## Why

Inputs arriving during turn finalization could be queued after the final batch had already been drained, or recorded ahead of that batch.

## What changed

Mark active turns as finishing before draining pending input. Reject injection into finishing turns and make late client responses and notifications wait until the final batch is recorded before appending to history. Continue accepting input into turns reserved but not yet started.

## Testing

Extend the task-completion test to block final recording, verify that input admission is closed, and confirm that a late notification is recorded after queued input while preserving the notification truncation budget. Strengthen the retained-tool-output scenario to assert tool output names and ordering.

GitOrigin-RevId: a57e44bd974e60e134183dab989795e2c3538596

Treat incomplete responses as terminal errors (#53451)

## Why

Incomplete responses such as `max_output_tokens` were classified as stream errors, allowing retries and compaction model fallback after the response had hit its output limit.

## What changed

Introduce `ResponseIncomplete` errors that preserve the server-provided reason and stop stream processing immediately. Make these errors non-retryable and stop compaction without falling back to the selected model. Record incomplete responses separately in sampler failure metrics.

## Testing

Add regression tests that verify incomplete responses surface a terminal error without retries over SSE and WebSocket, and that compaction stops without retrying or switching models for both local and remote compaction.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6e107d441b9bf03fa47ea47b88eeb94b71a9f729

Suppress repeated turn diffs in `codex exec` human output (#53444)

## Why

Repeated turn diff notifications can print the same file changes multiple times, including after an unrelated command.

## What changed

Track the last diff and print nonempty updates only when they differ from the previous notification. Remember empty updates so a restored diff prints again, and reset the tracked diff when a new turn starts.

## Testing

Add a stderr snapshot test covering repeated, changed, empty, restored, and new-turn diffs. Add an integration test that applies one edit, runs an unrelated command, and verifies that the diff appears exactly once.

## What changed

- Register the local x64 and ARM64 C++ toolchains in `ci-windows-msvc`.
- Apply `--config=ci-windows-msvc` to the native Windows Bazel test job.
- Allow the native Windows test job to run on `workflow_dispatch` as well as pushes to `main` so toolchain changes can be tested manually.

Create helpers under `CODEX_HOME/tmp/arg0-<os>` and limit stale-directory cleanup to that operating system's root. Keep permission discovery compatible with both the current platform's root and legacy `tmp/arg0` directories, while ignoring other platforms' aliases.

Add regression coverage for cleanup isolation, live helper preservation during legacy cleanup, and selection of the first session alias directory from either supported root.

## What changed

- Terminate V8 execution when `exit()` is called and complete the cell even if its module promise remains pending.
- Guard host callbacks against effects after exit, including when getters or value conversion request exit.
- Preserve stored writes made before exit and suppress errors when exit occurs during exception formatting.

## Testing

Add regression tests for synchronous and asynchronous exit, timers, parallel promises, value conversion, exception getters, and resuming after a yield and tool response. Verify that only prior output and stored writes survive, and separately exercise host guards while JavaScript continues running.
